title: The coded deferral reason, its code list and the review date have no column, no field list and no list of values in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-020 (AC1 'a coded reason and a review date'; Data table: recovery_case, queue, assignment, task, decision_log_entry, rule_row); FSD S4 v3 A2.20.3.1 (VR-S4-020-1, R-LIT-55, R-LIT-44, R-LIT-51, BR-S4-020) and A2.20.3.2 field catalogue (legal_action columns only); TSD S4 v2 T3.1 (legal_action DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014, hearing DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029, no deferral column) and T3.2 lists of values; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-55 (deferral_reason and deferral_review_date are both present)
section: Sections 3, 7, 11, 12.1, 13 and 14 of both stories and the fragment keys ops_provided and reqs
description: The deferral needs three things that no source specifies: the field that carries the coded reason, the field that carries the review date, and the code list the reason is drawn from. The legacy story names a coded reason and a review date and lists neither in its data table; the FSD field catalogue lists legal_action columns only; the TSD lists legal_action and hearing with no deferral column; the reference data of the module holds LOV-LEGAL-TYPE, LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, LOV-HEARING and LOV-HEARING-OUTCOME and no reason list. R-LIT-55 requires both elements but names no field type, no list and no storage. Both stories therefore carry the two elements as elements of the contract named after the rule, record them as facts of the decision record, and write no business column and no list value; the placeholder marks the gap in every table that names them.
evidence: The legacy data table of RWB-E5-020 lists recovery_case, queue, assignment, task, decision_log_entry and rule_row and no legal_action row; FSD S4 A2.20.3.2 lists legal_action.case_id, law_firm_id, action_type, lawsuit_no, black_case_no, red_case_no, court_name and claim_amount; TSD S4 T3.1 ends at DF-LEG-014 for legal_action; TSD S4 T3.2 lists four LOVs and none for a deferral reason; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-55 names deferral_reason and deferral_review_date in its condition column and no field definition
area: Data and reference data, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst of EP05 with the data steward of S4 and the reference-data owner of rwb-case
proposed: Keep the two elements as contract elements and decision-record facts with the element names R-LIT-55 uses, declare the reason list as a versioned reference value with the placeholder, and add no column to legal_action until the reference-data owner publishes the list

title: Three consumed owner contracts of the deferral step have no dependency row, and the plan gives both stories no contract or integration dependency
source: Template and Rules v1 §R5.4 dependency classes and §R5.5 DP table rows DP-03, DP-13 and DP-19; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5020-APP (Depends on (build) = RWB-S4-E5020-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON; Contract, Integration and External dependencies = None) and of RWB-S4-E5020-CON (all four None); the plan slice list of the legacy key; Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-litigation owns the legal action and the hearing) and slide 19 (rwb-litigation provides GET/PATCH /legal-actions and receives notices and partner results)
section: Sections 3, 12.2, 12.8, 12.9 and 19 of both stories and the fragment keys ops_consumed, C and I
description: Both stories consume three things that no metadata row carries: the case read of rwb-case (P3), the case answer that carries the stage move, the queue placement and the task request of rwb-case, and the rule package read of rwb-decision (P7). The ownership is unambiguous in the ownership rows, so none of the three can be turned into a table read without breaking DP-01 and DP-05, and no source names their operations. The metadata rows are kept exactly as the plan gives them, with Contract, Integration and External dependencies None, so the three rows are declared in 12.2 as consumed and faked and the Day-1 build order is unchanged. A reader of the metadata alone would conclude that the step needs only its own contract and the two platform contracts.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 R5.5: DP-03 adds H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-19 adds H RWB-PLT-N001-CON, DP-13 adds none; the patterns applied to both stories are DP03, DP13 and DP19 only; the metadata rows of both stories name no contract, integration or external dependency; the ownership rows of S4 give it five REST operations and one workflow and no queue, assignment or task row; the FSD A2.20.2 integration point is the Workbench alone and names no operation
area: Dependencies and contracts, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation with P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision
owner_role: Solution architect with the P3 and P7 owners
proposed: Build the two stories against the published documents and the fakes of the three consumed contracts on Day 1, keep the metadata rows as the plan gives them, and add the C rows at the next plan revision if the owners publish operation names

title: R-LIT-44 and the judgment write are named by two legacy keys, so the judgment criterion of RWB-E5-020 is a regression and not a second build
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-020 (AC3 Rule R-LIT-44) and heading RWB-E5-016 (AC2 Rule R-LIT-44, the same five lines); FSD S4 v3 A2.16 (judgment) and A2.20.3.1 (R-LIT-44 repeated in the deferral rule table); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-44; the metadata rows Depends on of both legacy stories (E5-020 depends on FEAT-LIT-16, E5-016 is that feature); the slice lists of RWB-E5-016 and RWB-E5-020 in _work/msr/plan/split_plan.json
section: Sections 2, 7, 8, 12 and 18 of both stories and the fragment key tcs
description: The same rule row R-LIT-44 and the same five criterion lines are carried by RWB-E5-016 and by RWB-E5-020, and the FSD repeats the rule in the deferral table of A2.20.3.1. Both keys are split in this run, so two application stories would each build a judgment write, a second stage move to JUDGMENT_RECORDED and a second enforcement task request on the same table and the same contract. The plan does not say which slice owns the behaviour. This WP resolves it by ownership of the build and not of the criterion: the four legacy criteria of RWB-E5-020 are owned word for word here, and the judgment path behind AC3 is declared as the behaviour of RWB-S4-E5016-APP on the same published contract, proved here as a regression. The contract baseline of this key declares no judgment element, no judgment operation and no second write, and its AC6 states the boundary.
evidence: The AC3 block of RWB-E5-020 and the AC2 block of RWB-E5-016 are the same four Given/When/Then lines under the same rule ID; FSD S4 A2.16 and A2.20.3.1 both list R-LIT-44; the legacy metadata of RWB-E5-020 names FEAT-LIT-16 as its prerequisite; TSD S4 T4 holds one row for R-LIT-44; the ownership rows give S4 two tables and five operations, so a second judgment write would land on the same legal_action row
area: Scope and traceability, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Solution architect with the tech lead of S4 and the business analyst of EP05
proposed: Keep R-LIT-44's criterion in both keys as the legacy gives it, build the judgment path once in RWB-S4-E5016-APP, prove AC3 here as a regression through the same contract, and declare the boundary in the CON absence test

title: The Workbench scheduler of R-LIT-55 has no equivalent in the target, and DP-10 is not in the pattern set of this key
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-55 (Systems: Workbench, Workbench scheduler; Timer: To the review date) and R-LIT-56, R-LIT-57; FSD S4 v3 A2.20.2 and A2.20.3.1; context pack S4 ownership rows (Jobs 0, Workflows 1: LitigationWorkflow); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10 (Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) against the patterns applied DP03, DP13 and DP19; TSD S4 v2 T4
section: Sections 4, 5, 8, 9, 12.5, 12.6 and 19 of both stories and the fragment key workflows
description: R-LIT-55 re-queues the case on the review date and names the Workbench scheduler as the system that does it, and R-LIT-56 returns the case to the enforcement decision when the date is reached. The monolith did that from its Quartz scheduler; the target has no scheduler row for this service, the ownership rows list zero jobs, and DP-10 is not in the pattern set of the key and would add a platform dependency that the plan does not carry. R-LIT-56 and R-LIT-57 are also not covered by any acceptance criterion of RWB-E5-020, so a reader cannot tell whether the return and the write-off routing are built here. This WP reads the re-queue as one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow, declares no Schedule, no Quartz row, no timer row and no shared job table, and leaves R-LIT-56 as the timer's own continuation and R-LIT-57 to rwb-writeoff.
evidence: The systems column of R-LIT-55 names the Workbench scheduler; the ownership rows of S4 give the service 0 jobs and 1 workflow; the patterns applied are DP03, DP13 and DP19, so no RWB-PLT-E1071-CON row is in the build list; the legacy story carries four criteria and none of them names R-LIT-56 or R-LIT-57; TSD S4 T4 lists R-LIT-56 and R-LIT-57 as LITIGATION rows of the shared machine
area: Scheduling and workflow, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Solution architect with the workflow platform owner and the tech lead of S4
proposed: Carry the review date as one durable timer of LitigationWorkflow on queue rwb-litigation, answer the return to ENFORCEMENT_DECISION under R-LIT-56 when it fires, declare no Schedule and no job row, and leave the second-deferral routing of R-LIT-57 to rwb-writeoff

title: SCR-20 carries no deferred state and no source gives a screen field list for the reason and the review date
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-020 (Screen and states: SCR-20 Enforcement workspace, Requested; seized; auctioned; closed; SCR-19 Litigation workspace, Pack; instructed; filed; hearing; judgment); FSD S4 v3 A2.20.3.3 (roles) and the SCR-20 row of the screen table; TSD S4 v2 T6.1; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-19
description: R-LIT-55 moves the case to DEFERRAL_RECORDED and the user records a reason and a review date on a screen, but the legacy state list of SCR-20 is Requested, seized, auctioned and closed and carries no deferred state, and no source gives the field list of the screen or the place where the reason and the date are shown. DP-19 routes SCR-20 through the gateway-bff composite route, and the screen model belongs to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the edge stories, so this WP cannot decide the field list. Both stories declare a deferred reading of SCR-20, name the four legacy states, record that the deferred state is added by this story, and leave the field list and the merge order to the route owner.
evidence: The screen table of RWB-E5-020 gives SCR-20 four states and none is a deferral; the FSD A2.20 names the screen in step 1 and gives no field list; the FSD screen table row for SCR-20 describes the enforcement steps with the Legal Execution Department and the result; TSD S4 T6.1 holds rights and no screen fields; DP-19 assigns the composite route and the merge to RWB-PLT-N001-CON
area: Screens and user interface, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation with RWB-PLT-N001
owner_role: Solution architect with the edge owner and the business analyst of EP05
proposed: Add a deferred reading to SCR-20 in the screen model, show the reason, the review date and the rule version there, and leave the field list and the merge order to RWB-PLT-N001-CON

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-020, so both stories trace to the feature and to the nearest module requirement
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-020 (metadata table: Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-20, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-LIT-16, Decision); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-020 with reqs = []; FSD S4 v3 requirements served (REQ-S4-007) and A2.20; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row FEAT-LIT-20
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories and the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-020 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-20 and the prerequisite FEAT-LIT-16 and no requirement row, and the plan's legacy index records an empty requirement list. The FSD S4 requirements table holds REQ-S4-007, 'Enforcement after judgment has one named owner from judgment to the end of enforcement', which is the requirement the feature serves and the sentence the feature's own problem statement repeats, but the mapping is made here and not by the source. Both stories trace to FEAT-LIT-20, to REQ-S4-007 and to the L3 process 08 Litigate and enforce. Nothing blocks the build; the exposure is a traceability report whose requirement link rests on a mapping the PRD of EP05 has not confirmed.
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-020 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index of the run records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 requirements served lists REQ-S4-007 with the text on one named owner of enforcement after judgment; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-20 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind User, Primary role Enforcement owner, Systems the Workbench, Depends on FEAT-LIT-16 and no requirement
area: Traceability and requirements, EP05, S4 rwb-litigation
owner_role: Business analyst of EP05 and the PRD owner of the epic
proposed: Trace both stories to FEAT-LIT-20, to REQ-S4-007 and to the L3 process 08, mark the link as a mapping, and rewrite it if the Epics 3 to 8 PRD names another requirement
